_about: L2-prep sample. A deliberately small, high-confidence set: every 'family' label is textbook-unambiguous, so any mismatch with a target's fetched rcsb_title is a curation bug I want to catch. This is a starting point designed to be extended toward 20-30 once the pipeline is proven. Curator assertions are 'family' and 'label' only.
_known_limitation: Redundancy: the three lysozyme_c entries (1HEL/6LYZ/1LYZ) are the SAME protein (hen egg-white lysozyme) in different crystal forms, and the two ubiquitin_like entries (1UBQ/1UBI) are both ubiquitin. Their within-family cosine is therefore trivially ~1.0 and inflates the overall within-family mean. The only family here with genuinely non-redundant members sharing a fold is globin (Hb α / Hb β / myoglobin). A real L2 benchmark must use non-redundant sequences per family; this starter set intentionally keeps the duplicates so the pipeline surfaces the issue.

_families.lysozyme_c: hen egg-white (c-type) lysozyme — NOT T4/phage lysozyme, which is an unrelated fold
_families.other: out-group: each entry is a distinct, unrelated protein
